\begin{center}
{\LARGE Ridge Broker Ablation Experiment}
\end{center}
\vspace{0.75em}

\paragraph{Question and design.}
These ablations probe three components of the broker's learning setup under
Ridge learning. They do not provide an additive decomposition of the broker's
advantage. The paired-Ridge reference pools the broker's mediated-match
history and uses additive and bilinear pair features. \emph{Size-matched pooled
history} retains these features but uses the smaller of the broker's available
sample and the median agent fitting-sample size. \emph{Single-principal history}
randomly retains one endpoint type from each mediated match for fitting; the
endpoint labels have no directional meaning. At prediction, the fitted
one-type function is applied to both parties and the fitting-sample output mean
is subtracted once. This variant produces an additive pair score and cannot
represent a bilinear interaction. \emph{Additive Ridge} retains both endpoint
types in every fitting row but replaces the pair features with their
type-vector sum, so it also cannot represent a bilinear interaction. The agent
learning rule and parameters are unchanged, but realized agent histories can
change as matching evolves. All conditions use $\lambda_a=0.003$,
$\lambda_b=0.001$, the same period window and fitting cadence, and the same
broker observation cap before any additional size matching.

The primary estimand in realization $c$ is the late-period broker-agent
holdout rank-correlation gap
\[
G_v(c)=\overline r_{b,v}(c)-\overline r_{a,v}(c),
\]
for Ridge broker variant $v$. The ablation contrast is
$G_v(c)-G_{\mathrm{pair}}(c)$. Each bar averages periods 481--500 within seed
and then averages seeds. The baseline comparisons use \rav{nBaselineSeeds}
common seeds. Other conditions use \rav{nOtherSeeds} common seeds. The
$\rho\times\delta$ analysis gives one observation to each of the
\rav{nConditions} effective realizations, including the baseline. Repeated
grid coordinates that map to the same realization receive no additional
weight. Because the ablations alter broker rankings, matches, and later
learning histories, their contrasts are system-level effects of the specified
restriction, not fixed-data comparisons of fitted regressions.

\paragraph{Results across effective realizations.}

the baseline and $\rho\times\delta$ design. Figure~\ref{fig:ridge-ablations}B--D
shows the paired realization contrasts, while
Figure~\ref{fig:ridge-ablation-grid} displays the $\rho\times\delta$ pattern
for each broker variant.
